title: Artesunate Targets MBL2 to Modulate the TLR4/NRF2/HO‑1 Axis and Ameliorate Podophyllotoxin‑Induced Liver Injury.
authors: Wei, Mingyue; He, Junjie; Zhang, Yanzhao; Chen, Hetao; Wang, Xue; Liu, Miaomiao; Chang, Jianying; Fan, Chunyang; Jiang, Hongwei; Liu, Chuanxin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究青蒿琥酯靶向MBL2调节TLR4/NRF2信号通路改善药物性肝损伤，虽含分子动力学模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) presents a significant clinical challenge with limited preventive and therapeutic options. Artesunate (ART) holds potential for DILI treatment; however, its precise hepatoprotective mechanisms and direct molecular target(s) remain unclear. METHODS: We evaluated ART in a podophyllotoxin (PPT)-induced rat model of DILI. Its direct target was identified through integrated chemical proteomics (pull-down/LC-MS/MS) followed by biophysical validation (SPR, MST) and molecular dynamics simulations. Mechanistic insights from hepatic transcriptomics (RNA-seq) were confirmed by Western blot, and extended with targeted metabolomics and 16S rRNA sequencing of gut microbiota. RESULTS: ART administration conferred significant hepatoprotection in the PPT-induced rat model, as evidenced by dose-dependent amelioration of key serum markers of liver injury (P < 0.05), attenuation of hepatic oxidative stress, and improved histopathological outcomes. Mechanistically, we identified mannose-binding lectin 2 (MBL2) as a direct, high-affinity target of ART (KD  approximately 3.84 microM). Upon binding to MBL2, ART suppressed the hepatic TLR4/NF-kappaB inflammatory axis and, in parallel, relieved NF-kappaB-mediated repression of NRF2, thereby cooperatively activating the NRF2-driven antioxidant defense program. Integrated multi-omics analysis further revealed that ART remodeled the gut microbiota, enriching beneficial genera including Lactobacillus, and that the abundance of these bacteria correlated positively with hepatic levels of antioxidant metabolites (P < 0.05), supporting a functional role of the gut-liver axis in its systemic protective effects. CONCLUSION: This study elucidates that ART alleviates DILI through targeting MBL2, thereby dually modulating the NF-kappaB/NRF2 signaling axis to simultaneously suppress inflammatory responses and enhance endogenous antioxidant defenses. These findings provide a novel and robust pharmacological basis for repositioning ART for the clinical prevention and treatment of DILI.
abstract_zh: 背景：药物性肝损伤（DILI）构成重大临床挑战，且预防和治疗选择有限。青蒿琥酯（ART）具有治疗DILI的潜力；然而，其精确的肝保护机制和直接分子靶点仍不清楚。方法：我们在鬼臼毒素（PPT）诱导的DILI大鼠模型中评估了ART。通过整合化学蛋白质组学（pull-down/LC-MS/MS）鉴定其直接靶点，随后进行生物物理验证（SPR、MST）和分子动力学模拟。来自肝脏转录组学（RNA-seq）的机制见解通过Western blot确认，并扩展至靶向代谢组学和肠道菌群16S rRNA测序。结果：ART给药在PPT诱导的大鼠模型中赋予显著肝保护作用，表现为肝损伤关键血清标志物的剂量依赖性改善（P < 0.05）、肝脏氧化应激的减轻以及组织病理学结果的改善。机制上，我们鉴定出甘露糖结合凝集素2（MBL2）为ART的直接高亲和力靶点（KD 约3.84微摩尔）。ART与MBL2结合后，抑制肝脏TLR4/NF-kappaB炎症轴，同时解除NF-kappaB对NRF2的抑制，从而协同激活NRF2驱动的抗氧化防御程序。整合多组学分析进一步揭示，ART重塑肠道菌群，富集包括乳杆菌属（Lactobacillus）在内的有益菌属，且这些细菌的丰度与肝脏抗氧化代谢物水平呈正相关（P < 0.05），支持肠-肝轴在其全身保护效应中的功能作用。结论：本研究阐明ART通过靶向MBL2缓解DILI，从而双重调节NF-kappaB/NRF2信号轴，同时抑制炎症反应并增强内源性抗氧化防御。这些发现为ART重新定位用于DILI的临床预防和治疗提供了新颖且坚实的药理学基础。
